harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured /tmp and /dev/shm on node1 to be mounted with noexec, nosuid, and nodev, persisted the settings via /etc/fstab, and verified the hardening survives a real reboot (confirmed by a changed boot_id).
actions_performed: Inspected baseline mount state of /tmp and /dev/shm and existing /etc/fstab
Backed up /etc/fstab before modification
Appended fstab entries mounting tmpfs at /tmp and /dev/shm with defaults,nosuid,nodev,noexec
Applied changes live via systemctl daemon-reload, mount -o remount /dev/shm, and mount /tmp
Verified noexec via failed script execution attempts on both mounts
Verified nodev via mknod succeeding but subsequent read access being denied
Verified nosuid/noexec combined effect via a setuid-copied binary failing to execute
Ran findmnt --verify to confirm no fstab errors
Captured pre-reboot boot_id and mount state baseline
Triggered a deferred sudo reboot so the acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until it reconnected after reboot
Confirmed boot_id changed, proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified /tmp and /dev/shm mount options and functional noexec enforcement post-reboot

evidence.requirement: /tmp and /dev/shm mounted noexec, nosuid, nodev before reboot
evidence.summary: Baseline showed /tmp not separately mounted and /dev/shm lacking noexec; added fstab entries and remounted live to apply noexec,nosuid,nodev to both.

evidence.requirement: Functional proof that exec, setuid, and device nodes are ignored on /tmp and /dev/shm
evidence.summary: Script execution denied on both /tmp and /dev/shm (noexec); mknod device node created but read access denied (nodev); setuid-copied binary in /tmp failed to execute (nosuid/noexec).

evidence.requirement: Settings persist in fstab / survive reboot config check
evidence.summary: /etc/fstab contains tmpfs entries for /tmp and /dev/shm with defaults,nosuid,nodev,noexec; findmnt --verify reported no errors for these entries.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory node-restart evidence protocol for node1: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, post-restart recovery
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id (28ae5f98...) and healthy mount state; issued deferred reboot with returned acknowledgement; node became unreachable then reconnected with new boot_id (deae565f...), proving a real restart; post-restart findmnt and exec tests confirm /tmp and /dev/shm retained noexec,nosuid,nodev and actively block script execution.

attempts.summary: Configured /tmp and /dev/shm on node1 to be mounted with noexec, nosuid, and nodev, persisted the settings via /etc/fstab, and verified the hardening survives a real reboot (confirmed by a changed boot_id).
